cards.title: A simple torch circuit
cards.idea: A cell pushes charge through a bulb. The push is voltage; the flow is current. A thin filament resists that flow.

interaction.prompt: Tap the bulb in the circuit to see what lights it up

cards.reveal: Charge flows from the cell, through the wire, into the filament. The filament glows because it resists the current and heats up.

cards.title: Push harder, flow faster
cards.idea: For a fixed resistor, more voltage means more current. Double the voltage and the current doubles too.

interaction.prompt: Slide the voltage from 0 V up to 6 V and watch the current reading

cards.reveal: Current rises in step with voltage. Their ratio stays constant. That fixed ratio is the resistance of the wire.

cards.title: Thin wire, thick wire
cards.idea: A thin, long wire resists flow more than a short, thick one, just like a narrow pipe slows water.

interaction.prompt: Tap the wire that lets more current through

cards.reveal: The thick short wire has lower resistance, so more current flows. Thin and long means higher resistance and dimmer glow.

cards.title: Naming the rule
cards.idea: Ohm's law: V = I R. Voltage equals current times resistance. Resistance R is measured in ohms, symbol omega.

interaction.prompt: Type the current when V = 6 V and R = 2 ohm

cards.reveal: I = V divided by R = 6 divided by 2 = 3 A. Rearranging V = I R gives current directly.

cards.title: When Ohm's law breaks
cards.idea: Ohmic conductors keep R constant, so V-I is a straight line. A bulb filament heats up, its R rises, and the line bends.

interaction.prompt: Tap the graph that shows an ohmic resistor

cards.reveal: The straight line is ohmic: R stays fixed. The curved one is the hot filament, where resistance grows as current increases.
